messages:
mike: Heads-up — we saw a single tenant saturate the ingress queue during EU primetime and push p95s above the SLO. Thinking we need a lightweight tenant-shed strategy that’s fair and cheap to evaluate. Anyone seen similar?

tara: Saw something like that last Q. Two levers: strict per-tenant caps vs probabilistic admission. Caps are simple but can leave spare capacity unused; probabilistic keeps them in but smooths spikes. :thinking:

yun: Important: streaming semantics. If we accept then drop midstream, we lose KV cache warmth and clients may retry aggressively. That increases churn.

mike: Constraints to satisfy: 1) keep tail latency for small/paid tenants, 2) avoid heavy global coordination, 3) provide easy signals to clients to back off. My straw proposal: per-tenant token-budget sliding window (cheap counters) + probabilistic admits once budget exceeded. Estimate tokens by request length/expected generation size.

tara: Agree on token-weighting (tokens ~ request_bytes + expected_response_tokens) rather than call-count. Also want a tiny guaranteed floor for enterprise "gold" tenants so they don't get fully drowned.

yun: Implementation notes: (a) Admission decision should be made at request start based on predicted cost. (b) If predicted_long_stream, only admit if bucket has >threshold to avoid midstream kills. (c) On drop, emit a short header like `X-RW-Shed: retry-after=100` so smart SDKs can respect a short backoff.

mike: Draft admit pseudo: ```window_ms=1000; tokens_limit=1000; tokens_used=atomic_inc(tenant); if tokens_used>tokens_limit: p= max(0, (tokens_limit - tokens_used)/tokens_limit); admit = random() < p else admit=true``` Cheap and avoids coordination.

tara: For fairness across tenants with different burst patterns, consider proportionally weighted reservoir admits: weight ~ committed_share or past-30s token-rate. That prevents huge tenants from hogging during short windows.

yun: Metrics to collect in experiments: p95 latency for small tenants, token-throttle-rate per-tenant, retry-after header hit rate, KV hit-rate delta while shedding. We should also trace shed decisions (span tag `shed=true`) so we can debug tail causes.

mike: Ops ops: Where to run this? I suggest implement as an ingress filter in frontdoor written in C++/fast path to minimize overhead. Make it configurable per-region and opt-out for dedicated tenants.

tara: Sim harness: I can wire up a quick sim that replays mixed tenant traces and tries caps vs probabilistic vs reservoir. Will include short-vs-long stream classification and naive retry model.

yun: Also add a short-lived token-bucket for long-lived streams so once admitted they charge incrementally rather than pre-reserving everything — that keeps burst protection without punishing long streams that already ran.

mike: Action items: mike -> write RFC w/ pseudocode + rollout plan; tara -> sampling sim harness; yun -> add trace tag + header support in gateway; ops-bot -> create experiment ticket and assign.

ops-bot: Created ticket INF-8421: "tenant-shed-experiment - probabilistic admission & long-stream safeguards" and linked this thread.
